    Brick-finiteness of E-finite algebras in rank at most two #

    Establishes the (E-fin) ⇔ brick-finite half of Theorem B / Theorem 8.4 (isEFinite_iff_brickFinite_of_rank_le_two and isEFinite_iff_brickFinite_right_of_rank_le_two). When n ≤ 2 and R is E-finite, Stern–Brocot subdivision covers the two mixed quadrants by finitely many compatible presilting cones, yielding finitely many weights at which every brick is stable.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.isEFinite_iff_positive_multiples_covered (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] :
    IsEFinite R ↔ ∀ (g : ProjectiveClass R), ∃ (p : ℕ) (P : TwoTerm R), 0 < p ∧ P.IsPresilting ∧ P.projectiveClass = p • g

    To test E-finiteness one may cover any positive multiple of each integral class. Stability is constant along a positive ray.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.isEFinite_of_integral_classes_in_presilting_sectors (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] (hc : ∀ (g : ProjectiveClass R), ∃ (E : TwoTerm R) (L : TwoTerm R), (E.directSum L).IsPresilting ∧ (realProjectiveClass R) g ∈ sectorBetween ((realProjectiveClass R) E.projectiveClass) ((realProjectiveClass R) L.projectiveClass)) :
    IsEFinite R

    A real sector cover by compatible pairs detects E-finiteness as soon as it contains the images of the integral classes.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.isEFinite_of_projective_rank_le_one (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] (hr : Module.finrank ℝ (RealProjectiveSpace R) ≤ 1) :
    IsEFinite R

    In a real projective class space of dimension at most one, the signed projective rays cover every integral class.
